title: How Tom Sawyer Turned Work into Play
subtitle: 湯姆如何把工作變成遊戲：馬克．吐溫的刷籬笆與說服術
source: 原創導讀；小說原文依 Project Gutenberg《The Adventures of Tom Sawyer》（1876，公版）第二章，心理學背景依 Wikipedia〈Overjustification effect〉，2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: Mark Twain, The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (1876), Project Gutenberg

beginner.title: The Fence
paras: It is a sunny Saturday morning. Tom Sawyer wants to play, but his Aunt Polly has given him a job: he must paint a long wooden fence white. The fence is thirty yards long and nine feet high. Tom feels very sad. Soon his friends will walk by and laugh at him.
這是個陽光明媚的星期六早上。湯姆．索亞想去玩，但他的波莉阿姨給了他一份工作：他必須把一道長長的木籬笆刷成白色。籬笆有三十碼長、九英尺高。湯姆非常沮喪。很快他的朋友們就會經過，還會嘲笑他。

Then Tom has a great idea. When his friend Ben comes by, eating an apple, Tom does not look sad at all. He paints slowly and carefully, as if it is the most interesting thing in the world. “Does a boy get a chance to whitewash a fence every day?” he asks.
接著湯姆想到一個好主意。當他的朋友班吃著蘋果經過時，湯姆一點也不顯得難過。他慢慢地、仔細地刷著，好像這是世界上最有趣的事。「一個男孩可不是每天都有機會刷籬笆的，對吧？」他問。

Ben becomes interested and asks to try. Tom says no — the job is too important! Ben begs and finally gives Tom his apple. Soon other boys come and pay Tom to paint: a kite, a dead rat, marbles and other treasures. By the afternoon, the fence has three coats of paint.
班開始感興趣，要求試試看。湯姆說不行——這份工作太重要了！班苦苦哀求，最後把蘋果給了湯姆。很快地，其他男孩也來了，付東西給湯姆換取刷籬笆的機會：一個風箏、一隻死老鼠、彈珠和其他寶貝。到了下午，籬笆已經刷了三層漆。

Mark Twain, who wrote this story in 1876, explains the lesson with a smile. Tom has discovered that if you want someone to want something, you just need to make it hard to get. Twain also says that work is what we must do, and play is what we do not have to do.
寫下這個故事的馬克．吐溫，在 1876 年帶著微笑說明了其中的道理。湯姆發現：如果你想讓別人想要某樣東西，只要讓它很難得到就行了。吐溫還說，工作是我們必須做的事，而遊戲是我們不必做的事。

Today, psychologists study similar ideas. Some studies suggest that if we are paid for something we already enjoy, we may start to enjoy it less. So the next time you have a boring job, ask yourself: is it really boring, or does it only feel that way because you have to do it?
今天，心理學家研究類似的概念。一些研究顯示，如果我們做一件本來就喜歡的事卻開始拿到報酬，我們可能會變得沒那麼喜歡它。所以下次你遇到一份無聊的工作時，問問自己：它真的很無聊嗎？還是只是因為你「必須」做，才覺得無聊？

intermediate.title: How Tom Sawyer Turned Work into Play
paras: On a bright Saturday morning, Tom Sawyer appears with a bucket of whitewash and a long-handled brush. Before him stands thirty yards of board fence, nine feet high, which Aunt Polly has ordered him to whitewash. All his happiness disappears. Soon the other boys will pass on their way to fun, and they will laugh at him for having to work.
一個晴朗的星期六早上，湯姆．索亞拿著一桶白漆和一把長柄刷子出現了。他面前是一道三十碼長、九英尺高的木板籬笆，波莉阿姨命令他把它刷白。他所有的快樂都消失了。很快地，其他男孩會在去玩的路上經過，還會嘲笑他得工作。

Tom considers paying someone to help, but his possessions — bits of toys, marbles and rubbish — are not enough to buy even half an hour of freedom. Then, as Mark Twain writes, “an inspiration burst upon him”. When his friend Ben Rogers comes along eating an apple, Tom pretends to be absorbed in his work. Asked whether he is really working, he replies: “Does a boy get a chance to whitewash a fence every day?”
湯姆考慮過付錢請人幫忙，但他的家當——一些玩具碎片、彈珠和破爛——連買半小時的自由都不夠。接著，正如馬克．吐溫所寫，「一個靈感突然湧上他的心頭」。當他的朋友班．羅傑斯吃著蘋果走過來時，湯姆假裝全神貫注於工作。被問到他是不是真的在工作時，他回答：「一個男孩可不是每天都有機會刷籬笆的，對吧？」

The question changes everything. Ben stops eating his apple and watches Tom’s careful brushstrokes with growing interest. When Ben asks to try, Tom refuses, explaining that Aunt Polly is “awful particular about this fence” and that hardly one boy in a thousand could do it properly. Ben offers the core of his apple, then the whole apple. Other boys follow, trading a kite, a dead rat and many other treasures for a turn.
這個問題改變了一切。班停止吃蘋果，越來越感興趣地看著湯姆仔細的每一刷。班要求試試時，湯姆拒絕了，解釋說波莉阿姨對這道籬笆「挑剔得要命」，一千個男孩裡大概找不到一個能把它刷好。班先拿出蘋果核，接著是整顆蘋果。其他男孩也接踵而來，用一個風箏、一隻死老鼠和許多其他寶貝來換一次刷籬笆的機會。

By mid-afternoon, Tom has spent an idle, pleasant day, the fence has three coats of whitewash, and he is “literally rolling in wealth”. Twain then states the lesson with gentle irony. Tom has discovered “a great law of human action”: to make someone want a thing, “it is only necessary to make the thing difficult to attain.” Work, Twain adds, is whatever we are obliged to do; play is whatever we are not obliged to do.
到了午後，湯姆悠閒愉快地度過了一天，籬笆刷了三層白漆，而他「簡直富得流油」。吐溫接著以溫和的反諷點出教訓：湯姆發現了「人類行為的一條偉大法則」——要讓人想要一樣東西，「只要讓那樣東西難以得到就行了」。吐溫補充說，工作就是我們不得不做的事；遊戲就是我們不必做的事。

Modern psychology has explored ideas that echo Twain’s joke. Research on the “overjustification effect” suggests that offering expected rewards, such as money or prizes, for an activity people already enjoy can sometimes reduce their own interest in it. Tom’s trick works the other way round: by making the task seem like a privilege, he turns a chore into something the boys want to pay for.
現代心理學探討了一些與吐溫的玩笑相呼應的觀念。關於「過度辯證效應」的研究顯示，對人們本來就喜歡的活動提供預期中的獎勵，例如金錢或獎品，有時反而會降低他們自己的興趣。湯姆的把戲正好反過來運作：他把這項任務包裝成一種特權，把一份苦差事變成男孩們願意付錢來做的事。

advanced.title: The Great Law of Human Action
paras: The second chapter of Mark Twain’s The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, published in 1876, contains one of the most famous lessons in persuasion in American literature. On a glorious Saturday morning, Tom confronts “thirty yards of board fence nine feet high” that he has been ordered to whitewash. Twain renders his despair with comic grandeur: life seems “hollow, and existence but a burden”, and the small whitewashed streak looks insignificant beside “the far-reaching continent of unwhitewashed fence”.
馬克．吐溫 1876 年出版的《湯姆歷險記》第二章，包含了美國文學中最著名的說服課之一。在一個燦爛的星期六早上，湯姆面對著「三十碼長、九英尺高的木板籬笆」，他被命令把它刷白。吐溫以滑稽的誇張筆法描寫他的絕望：生活似乎「空洞，存在不過是負擔」，而那一小道刷白的痕跡，在「一望無際、尚未刷白的籬笆大陸」旁邊顯得微不足道。

Tom first contemplates bribery, but his worldly wealth — “bits of toys, marbles, and trash” — could not buy “so much as half an hour of pure freedom”. His solution is subtler: he changes not the task but its meaning. When Ben Rogers, the boy “whose ridicule he had been dreading”, arrives impersonating a steamboat, Tom ignores him and works with the absorption of an artist. The decisive line reframes the situation entirely: “Does a boy get a chance to whitewash a fence every day?”
湯姆一開始考慮賄賂，但他的全部財產——「玩具碎片、彈珠和破爛」——連「半小時純粹的自由」都買不起。他的解決辦法更巧妙：他改變的不是任務本身，而是任務的意義。當班．羅傑斯——那個「他一直害怕被他嘲笑」的男孩——模仿著汽船出現時，湯姆不理會他，以藝術家般的專注工作著。關鍵的一句話徹底重新框定了情境：「一個男孩可不是每天都有機會刷籬笆的，對吧？」

What follows is a masterclass in manufactured scarcity. Tom steps back to admire his brushwork, adds “a touch here and there” and, when Ben asks to try, refuses on the grounds that Aunt Polly is “awful particular about this fence” and that perhaps not one boy in a thousand could do it properly. Exclusivity transforms drudgery into a prize. Ben surrenders his apple, and a procession of boys who “came to jeer, but remained to whitewash” pays Tom in kites, marbles and a dead rat, until he has become, from a poor boy in the morning, one “literally rolling in wealth”.
接下來是一堂製造稀缺性的大師課。湯姆退後一步欣賞自己的筆觸，「這裡那裡補上一筆」，當班要求試試時，他以波莉阿姨對這道籬笆「挑剔得要命」、一千個男孩裡也許找不到一個能刷好為由拒絕了。排他性把苦差事變成了獎品。班交出了他的蘋果，一群「來嘲笑、卻留下來刷籬笆」的男孩接連用風箏、彈珠和一隻死老鼠付給湯姆，直到他從早上那個窮小子，變成了一個「簡直富得流油」的人。

Twain then steps forward as narrator to draw the moral, with characteristic irony. Tom “had discovered a great law of human action, without knowing it—namely, that in order to make a man or a boy covet a thing, it is only necessary to make the thing difficult to attain.” A wiser philosopher, Twain adds, would have understood that work “consists of whatever a body is obliged to do”, and play of whatever a body is not obliged to do. He offers a final example: wealthy English gentlemen pay to drive passenger coaches for pleasure, but if they were offered wages, “that would turn it into work and then they would resign.”

接著，吐溫以敘事者身分站出來點出寓意，帶著他一貫的反諷。湯姆「在不知不覺中發現了一條人類行為的偉大法則——那就是，要讓一個男人或男孩渴望一樣東西，只要讓那樣東西難以得到就行了」。吐溫補充說，一位更有智慧的哲學家會明白，工作「就是一個人不得不做的任何事」，而遊戲就是一個人不必做的任何事。他舉了最後一個例子：富有的英國紳士花錢駕駛載客馬車取樂，但如果付他們工資，「那就會把它變成工作，然後他們就會辭職」。

That last observation anticipates a theme later studied by psychologists under the name of the overjustification effect: offering expected external rewards for an activity that is already intrinsically enjoyable can, in some circumstances, reduce people’s motivation to do it. Researchers continue to debate how strongly such laboratory findings apply to real life. Twain’s chapter, however, captures the core insight with remarkable economy. How we frame an activity — as obligation or opportunity, chore or privilege — can matter as much as the activity itself.
最後這個觀察，預示了後來心理學家以「過度辯證效應」之名研究的主題：對一項本身就令人愉快的活動提供預期中的外在獎勵，在某些情況下，反而會降低人們從事它的動機。研究者至今仍在爭論，這類實驗室發現在多大程度上適用於現實生活。然而，吐溫的這一章以驚人的精簡捕捉了核心洞見：我們如何框定一項活動——是義務還是機會，是苦差事還是特權——可能和活動本身一樣重要。

quote.text: In order to make a man or a boy covet a thing, it is only necessary to make the thing difficult to attain.
quote.author: Mark Twain
quote.work: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (1876), Chapter 2

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Ben learned to eat his apples more slowly.
How to paint a long fence quickly and well.
Why Aunt Polly liked fences that were painted white.
How Tom made a boring job look like a rare chance.
beginner.evidence: Does a boy get a chance to whitewash a fence every day?
beginner.why: 全文：湯姆把苦差事包裝成難得的機會。
traps: 字面誤讀：蘋果只是交換的報酬。
捏造：故事重點不是刷油漆技巧。
捏造：文中沒提她的喜好。

beginner.q: What does “it” in “asks to try” and “Tom says no — the job is too important” refer to?
options: Eating the apple.
Painting the fence.
Flying a kite.
Counting marbles.
beginner.evidence: Ben becomes interested and asks to try.
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：蘋果是交換的東西。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：風箏是其他男孩的報酬。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：彈珠是報酬之一。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Tom paid his friends to help him paint.
The fence was nine yards long.
By the afternoon, the fence had three coats of paint.
Mark Twain wrote the story in 1867.
beginner.evidence: By the afternoon, the fence has three coats of paint.
traps: 正反顛倒：是朋友付東西給湯姆。
數字錯位：三十碼長、九呎高。
數字錯位：1876 年。

beginner.q: According to Twain, what makes people want something?
options: Making it hard to get.
Making it free for all.
Making it very easy.
Making it look sad.
beginner.evidence: if you want someone to want something, you just need to make it hard to get
traps: 正反顛倒：湯姆讓它變得難得。
正反顛倒：要讓它難以得到。
正反顛倒：湯姆刻意看起來很享受。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Tom made a chore seem like a privilege others would pay for.
Tom worked hard all day to finish the fence alone.
Ben Rogers tricked Tom into giving away his apple.
Aunt Polly paid the other boys to paint the fence.
intermediate.evidence: by making the task seem like a privilege, he turns a chore into something the boys want to pay for
traps: 正反顛倒：他整天悠閒，別人替他刷。
張冠李戴：是 Ben 把蘋果給湯姆。
捏造：文中沒有。是男孩付東西給湯姆。

intermediate.q: What does Tom mean when he says Aunt Polly is “awful particular about this fence”?
options: She is afraid of the fence falling down.
She hates the color of the fence.
She cares very much about how it is painted.
She has forgotten about the fence.
intermediate.evidence: Tom refuses, explaining that Aunt Polly is “awful particular about this fence”
intermediate.why: particular＝講究、挑剔，所以不是誰都能刷。
traps: 捏造：文中沒提籬笆會倒。
字面誤讀：awful 在這裡是「非常」，不是討厭。
正反顛倒：她其實非常在意。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Ben offered Tom a kite before anything else he had.
Tom’s things could not buy even half an hour of freedom.
Tom finished painting the whole fence by himself.
The fence was given only two coats of whitewash.
intermediate.evidence: are not enough to buy even half an hour of freedom
traps: 張冠李戴：Ben 給的是蘋果，風箏是別的男孩。
正反顛倒：是其他男孩替他刷。
數字錯位：原文是刷了三層。

intermediate.q: What does research on the “overjustification effect” suggest?
options: Prizes can make every boring job fun to do.
People always work much harder when they are paid.
Painting fences is very good exercise for children.
Rewards for something we enjoy can reduce our interest.
intermediate.evidence: offering expected rewards, such as money or prizes, for an activity people already enjoy can sometimes reduce their own interest in it
traps: 正反顛倒：獎勵不會讓無聊的事變有趣。
正反顛倒：有時反而降低興趣。
捏造：文中沒談運動的好處。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To describe the history of whitewash in America.
To show how framing can turn work into something like play.
To prove that bribery always works with young children.
To explain how steamboats were built in the year 1876.
advanced.evidence: How we frame an activity — as obligation or opportunity, chore or privilege — can matter as much as the activity itself.
traps: 捏造：文中沒談石灰漆的歷史。
正反顛倒：湯姆放棄賄賂，改變的是意義。
字面誤讀：Ben 只是在模仿汽船。

advanced.q: What does “manufactured scarcity” in the third paragraph refer to?
options: Running out of whitewash before the job was done.
Building a fence out of scarce and costly wood.
Selling paint to the boys at a high price.
Making something seem rare so that people want it.
advanced.evidence: Exclusivity transforms drudgery into a prize.
advanced.why: 湯姆刻意說一千個男孩裡也許沒一個做得好，人為製造稀有感。
traps: 字面誤讀：漆並沒有用完。
字面誤讀：manufacture 不是真的建造。
捏造：沒人賣油漆。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The boys who came to jeer stayed to whitewash.
Tom first tried to make Ben jealous with marbles.
Twain said English gentlemen were paid to drive coaches.
The story appears in the first chapter of the novel.
advanced.evidence: came to jeer, but remained to whitewash
traps: 捏造：他先想過賄賂，但沒用彈珠引誘 Ben。
正反顛倒：他們是自己付錢去駕車。
數字錯位：原文是第二章。

advanced.q: Why would the English gentlemen resign if they were offered wages?
options: They did not know how to drive coaches.
The wages would be far too low for them.
Being paid would turn their pleasure into work.
Their families would not allow it.
advanced.evidence: if they were offered wages, “that would turn it into work and then they would resign.”
traps: 正反顛倒：他們很樂於駕車。
捏造：文中沒提薪水高低。
捏造：文中沒提家人。

reflections: Think of an activity you love doing for fun. Would you still enjoy it if you were paid or graded for it? Why or why not?
Is Tom clever, dishonest, or both? Give reasons for your answer.

湯姆先想到付錢請人幫忙，但他的「家當」——「玩具碎片、彈珠和破爛」——連半小時的自由都買不到。他的辦法更聰明：他改變的不是工作，而是工作的意義。當他最怕被嘲笑的班．羅傑斯啃著蘋果走過來時，湯姆不理他，像藝術家一樣專心工作。被問到是不是真的在幹活，他回答：「哪個男孩能天天有機會刷籬笆？」

What follows is a lesson in creating scarcity. When Ben asks to try, Tom refuses, explaining that Aunt Polly is “awful particular about this fence” and that perhaps not one boy in a thousand could do it properly. So effective is this refusal that Ben hands over his apple for a turn, and a stream of boys who “came to jeer, but remained to whitewash” pays Tom in kites, marbles and even a dead rat. By the afternoon, the fence has three coats of whitewash, and Tom is “literally rolling in wealth”.
接下來是一堂「製造稀有」的課。班想試試看時，湯姆拒絕了，說波麗姨媽「對這道籬笆講究得要命」，大概一千個男孩裡也沒一個能刷得好。這個拒絕效果好到班交出蘋果換一次機會，接著一群「來嘲笑、卻留下來刷籬笆」的男孩，用風箏、彈珠甚至一隻死老鼠付給湯姆。到了下午，籬笆刷了三層白漆，而湯姆「簡直富得流油」。

Twain then steps forward to state the moral with gentle irony. Tom, he says, had discovered “a great law of human action”: to make someone want a thing, “it is only necessary to make the thing difficult to attain.” Work, Twain adds, is whatever a person is obliged to do, and play is whatever a person is not obliged to do. Wealthy English gentlemen pay to drive passenger coaches for pleasure, yet if they were offered wages, “that would turn it into work and then they would resign.”
接著吐溫親自出面，以溫和的反諷點出寓意。他說，湯姆發現了「人類行為的一大法則」：要讓人想要某樣東西，「只需要讓它難以得到」。吐溫補充說，工作就是一個人「必須」做的事，玩樂則是「不必」做的事。富有的英國紳士付錢駕駛載客馬車當作消遣，但如果有人付他們薪水，「那就會變成工作，他們就會辭職了」。

That last joke anticipates what psychologists later called the overjustification effect: offering expected rewards for an activity people already enjoy can sometimes reduce their own interest in it. Researchers still debate how strongly such findings apply to real life. It was Twain, however, who caught the core idea with remarkable economy. How we frame an activity, as a chore or as a privilege, can matter as much as the activity itself.
最後那個笑話，預示了心理學家後來所說的「過度合理化效應」：為人們本來就喜歡的活動提供預期中的獎勵，有時反而會降低他們自己的興趣。研究者仍在爭論這類發現在現實生活中適用到什麼程度。然而，吐溫以驚人的精簡抓住了核心概念：我們如何框架一件事——當成苦差還是特權——可能和那件事本身一樣重要。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Tom turned a chore into a privilege others paid for.
How to whitewash a long wooden fence properly.
Why Aunt Polly was particular about her fence.
How English gentlemen learned to drive coaches.
questions.evidence: he changes not the task but its meaning
questions.why: 全文：湯姆改變工作的意義，讓別人搶著付錢刷籬笆，以及吐溫點出的寓意。
traps: 捏造：重點不是刷漆技巧。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：那是湯姆的說詞，不是重點。
以偏概全：紳士只是第四段的例子。

questions.q: What does “obliged” mean in the fourth paragraph?
options: Paid well to do something.
Happy to do something.
Required to do something.
Too tired to do something.
questions.evidence: Work, Twain adds, is whatever a person is obliged to do
questions.why: 和「玩樂是不必做的事」對照：必須做。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：薪水是紳士例子裡的條件。
正反顛倒：那比較接近玩樂。
捏造：obliged 跟累不累沒有關係。

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The fence was nine yards long and thirty feet high.
The fence was given three coats of whitewash.
Tom paid the other boys to paint the fence.
Ben offered Tom a kite before his apple.
questions.evidence: the fence has three coats of whitewash
traps: 數字錯位：三十碼長、九呎高。
正反顛倒：是男孩們付東西給湯姆。
時序錯置：班先交出蘋果，風箏是其他男孩給的。

questions.q: Why does Twain mention the English gentlemen who drive coaches?
options: To describe the rich people Tom wanted to meet.
To prove that coaches were common in America.
To explain how Tom earned his marbles.
To show how pay can turn play into work.
questions.evidence: if they were offered wages, “that would turn it into work and then they would resign.”
questions.why: 作者手法：用紳士的例子說明「付錢會讓玩樂變成工作」。
traps: 捏造：文中沒說湯姆想見有錢人。
捏造：文中沒提美國的馬車。
張冠李戴：彈珠是男孩們給湯姆的。

Tom’s possessions could not buy half an hour of freedom.
